answer: A terraced stake ladder resists sybil farms: each new agent must lock a refundable deposit to climb from the base terrace toward the summit, and the deposit only unlocks in small slices as peers verify real completed work. One identity costs little, but an ocean of fake agents must each pay the full deposit up front, and clones that do no useful work never recover it. The cost scales linearly with the number of identities while honest agents get their stake back, so a sybil farm bleeds money while a single real agent pays almost nothing.
